Hi all —

We located the incoming EUR payment in our bank feed. Bank reference: RB-20270411-9823. The amount received (EUR 42,350) matches Invoice 4821 when converted at the bank execution rate; conversion difference is EUR 23.45 (posting as FX gain).

We also received a separate credit note reference from Aegis (CN-2027-155) for USD 12,400 that your AP team included in the description. Because the credit note is denominated in USD and Invoice 4822 is a USD invoice, best-practice is to apply the credit directly to Invoice 4822 on the ledger and then post an FX revaluation entry to capture the conversion impact between the credit-note value and the EUR flow. That keeps VAT on the invoice intact for auditors.

Attached: MT103_SWIFT_20270411.txt (bank trace extract) — contains the sender reference and value date. I have redacted full account numbers for security.

Next steps I propose:
- We will apply EUR 42,350 to Invoice 4821 and mark it paid.
- We will apply USD 12,400 credit to Invoice 4822 and post an FX revaluation of the small rounding difference to the FX adjustment account.
- We will generate a certified Statement of Account with per-invoice VAT lines and a short explanatory note about FX reallocation.

If Aegis would prefer that we instead net the credit against the EUR receipt (i.e., convert USD credit into EUR and allocate against 4821), please advise within 48 hours — otherwise we will proceed with the ledger treatment above and issue the updated statement by EOD Tue.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Accounting Analyst
